The patient presents with new-onset ataxic gait and coordination ataxia, with peers describing them as "appearing drunk" — a classic cerebellar presentation. MRI shows multifocal demyelinating lesions without gadolinium enhancement, interpreted as consistent with PML, in the cerebellum/posterior fossa distribution. The key predisposing factor is natalizumab use for the past year — natalizumab is a well-known cause of PML (JC virus reactivation), particularly after ~2 years of therapy or with prior immunosuppression. The subacute, non-enhancing, multifocal demyelinating pattern fits PML.
